title: Testament of Abraham — Hobah Translation
about: A Jewish testamentary tale in which the archangel Michael is sent to announce Abraham's death. Abraham resists dying, receives a heavenly tour, witnesses judgment, and finally yields his spirit.

translation.base_text: Greek long recension (Recension A) in M. R. James, The Testament of Abraham (Cambridge, 1892), public-domain Greek edition
translation.method: Fresh modern-English rendering from the Greek long recension, with James's public-domain apparatus used to identify difficult readings. No modern copyrighted translation is copied.
translation.confidence: Medium-high for Recension A; lower where the manuscripts differ sharply or the Greek is corrupt
translation.notes: The long recension is translated as its own textual witness. The short recension is not silently blended into it.
translation.license_note: Ancient text and the 1892 Greek edition are public domain. Hobah English wording is newly prepared for this project.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.text: Abraham lived to the full measure of his days, righteous, hospitable, and merciful. When the time appointed for his death drew near, God said to the chief captain Michael, ‘Go down to Abraham my beloved and tell him that he must set his house in order, for he is about to leave the body and come to me.’ Michael descended and found Abraham sitting beneath a tree near his fields.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.text: Abraham saw the stranger and, as was his custom, rose to welcome him. ‘Come, my lord, into the house of your servant. Wash your feet, rest, and eat bread, and afterward you may continue your journey.’ Michael entered with him but was troubled, because he did not know how to speak the bitter message to one whom God loved so greatly.

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.text: Abraham called Isaac and said, ‘My son, draw water so that we may wash the feet of this traveller.’ When Isaac looked upon Michael, his heart was moved and he wept without knowing why. Michael also wept, and his tears became precious stones. Abraham secretly gathered them, marveling at the mystery.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.text: Sarah prepared food. At the meal Michael did not eat as a mortal eats, but by God's command he appeared to take food so that Abraham would not be alarmed. Afterward Abraham asked the guest his name and homeland. Michael answered cautiously, saying that he was a traveller and servant of the Most High.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.text: That night Isaac dreamed of a glorious man taking the sun from his father's head. He woke crying and told the dream to Abraham. Abraham and Sarah understood that some great separation was near, though they did not yet know the angel's message.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.text: Michael returned to heaven and said, ‘Lord, I cannot tell Abraham that he must die. I have never seen a man like him: compassionate, generous, and righteous. Command another way.’ God answered, ‘Go again. I will place the message in Isaac's heart through a dream, and Abraham will understand.’

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.text: Michael returned. Isaac recounted his dream before the household. Sarah recognized Michael, for she remembered the heavenly visitors who had announced Isaac's birth. She said to Abraham, ‘Do you not know this man? This is one of the three holy men who came to us at Mamre.’ Abraham then knew that his guest was an angel of God.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.text: Michael told Abraham, ‘God says: You have completed the years appointed to you. Leave the affairs of this life and come to your Lord.’ Abraham answered, ‘I will not yet go. Before I die, I ask to see the whole inhabited world and the works of human beings.’ Michael brought the request before God, and God granted it.

chapters.label: Chapter 9
chapters.text: A chariot of cherubim came down in great glory. Abraham and Michael entered it and were carried over the earth. Abraham saw people ploughing and sowing, travelling, feasting, marrying, arguing, trading, and working. He saw both acts of kindness and acts of wickedness.

chapters.label: Chapter 10
chapters.text: When Abraham saw thieves preparing murder, he cried, ‘Lord, let wild beasts devour them!’ and it happened. Seeing people committing sexual wickedness, he called for the earth to swallow them, and it did. Seeing others about to do evil, he asked that fire consume them. Michael was distressed by Abraham's severity and carried him away.

chapters.label: Chapter 11
chapters.text: God said, ‘Michael, bring Abraham back. He has not yet learned my compassion. If I repaid every sinner at once, none would survive to repent. I wait patiently so that the sinner may turn and live.’ Abraham was then shown a place with two gates, one broad and one narrow, through which souls passed.

chapters.label: Chapter 12
chapters.text: Between the gates sat a majestic man who sometimes laughed and sometimes wept. Michael explained, ‘This is Adam, the first-formed. When he sees many souls entering the broad gate to destruction, he weeps. When he sees souls entering the narrow gate to life, he rejoices.’

chapters.label: Chapter 13
chapters.text: They came to the place of judgment. Abel sat as judge, because every human being would first be judged by a human being. Enoch stood as scribe, recording righteous deeds and sins. Angels held books, while another angel weighed souls in a balance and another tested works by fire.

chapters.label: Chapter 14
chapters.text: Abraham saw a soul whose good and evil deeds were equal. The soul stood in uncertainty, neither condemned nor admitted to life. Abraham was moved with pity and prayed. Because of his intercession, the soul was received among the saved. Abraham then understood the power of mercy and prayer.

chapters.label: Chapter 15
chapters.text: He remembered the people he had condemned during his tour of the earth and repented of his harsh words. ‘I have sinned, Lord, because I judged sinners before their time.’ God restored those whose punishment had come through Abraham's angry requests, teaching him that divine patience seeks repentance rather than immediate destruction.

chapters.label: Chapter 16
chapters.text: Michael brought Abraham home. Yet Abraham still said, ‘I will not go with you.’ God therefore sent Death, adorned in beauty so that Abraham would not be terrified. Death stood before Abraham like a radiant youth, but Abraham perceived something strange and asked who he was.

chapters.label: Chapter 17
chapters.text: Death answered, ‘I am the bitter cup of death.’ Abraham said, ‘Show me your true form.’ Death warned him that no mortal could look upon it and remain unharmed, but Abraham insisted. Death then revealed many terrifying faces: serpent, sword, fire, fierce beast, storm, and every manner by which human beings die.

chapters.label: Chapter 18
chapters.text: Servants in Abraham's house saw the terrible appearance and fell dead in great number. Abraham rebuked Death: ‘Why have you killed my household?’ Death answered that Abraham himself had demanded to see the hidden form. Abraham prayed to God, and those who had fallen were restored to life.

chapters.label: Chapter 19
chapters.text: Death hid his frightening appearance and became beautiful again. Abraham said, ‘Tell me how you take the souls of the righteous.’ Death answered, ‘For the righteous my appearance is gentle, and I receive them in peace. For sinners I come according to the fear and bitterness appointed to their deeds.’

chapters.label: Chapter 20
chapters.text: At last Abraham lay down upon his bed. Death approached, but Abraham still resisted. God sent Michael with a message of peace. Then Abraham kissed the angel's hand, and Death took the soul through the kiss without violence. Michael received Abraham's soul in a shining cloth and carried it to heaven. God welcomed his friend and placed him among the righteous, where there is no grief, pain, or death, but life and peace forever.
